reduced-order forecast compression: 39-year SST -> POD spatial modes -> forecast time coefficients -> future SST -> species bands

territorial restriction update: foreign-water restriction -> route intersection -> earlier trigger -> company loss claim

global_organization_chain: Summary compresses SST snapshots -> three POD modes -> coefficient forecast -> species temperature envelopes -> freshness-limited ranges -> critical years -> three strategies -> territorial revision.
Introduction names the management audience, establishes the local livelihood stake, and converts the official prompt into four visible task bullets.
Problem 1 moves from field-wide forecast rationale through PCA/POD steps, a chronological holdout, coefficient extrapolation, and separate herring/March and mackerel/August maps.
Problem 2 turns biochemical explanation into two first-order Arrhenius indicators, threshold storage times, species-season radii, and three critical-year cases.
Problem 3 uses those dates to trigger a paired-port relocation map and NPV, a cold-chain vessel split, and a transit-station option.
Problem 4 qualitatively applies a Danish-water restriction; sensitivity and strengths/weaknesses qualify the chain before the one-page public article restates results and options.
References and the one-table appendix expose the source and reproduction boundary rather than silently filling omitted equations, data, code, or cash flows.

main_argument_chains.claim: A reduced-order SST forecast can locate future temperature-qualified habitat for the two species.
support_steps: Center and decompose covariance into spatial modes and time coefficients.
Retain three modes and extrapolate their coefficients.
Reconstruct future SST and apply species/month temperature bands.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The resulting envelopes identify where companies may need to follow herring and mackerel, subject to missing population and forecast uncertainty.

support_steps: Invert indicator maxima to storage time.

warnings.warning: The source is called a daily OISST dataset, but the modeled records are monthly snapshots; the daily-to-monthly aggregation is not disclosed.
The exact NOAA file, variable, version revision, download, land mask, missing-value rule, and preprocessing code are not published.
One-degree longitude-latitude cells have unequal physical area, but the vectorization and covariance give every cell equal weight.
The date range December 1981 through January 2020 contains 458 months, not the printed m=468 snapshots.
The first-446 plus last-12 split also totals 458, independently contradicting m=468.
The prose calls snapshots row vectors while the notation first displays a transposed stack; matrix orientation is not stated consistently in words.
No cell coordinate ledger or ocean/land mask is bundled, so the 680-vector cannot be reconstructed from the report.
The spatial domain is large enough to include coast and land boundaries, yet no rule explains how non-ocean cells enter covariance or maps.
The mean snapshot S_bar is not defined as a temporal mean over training data, full data, or another reference.
Future absolute SST reconstruction requires adding S_bar back, but the forecast discussion only says coefficients are multiplied by eigenvectors.
POD is described as discarding random-event impacts, although variance-optimal modes can retain high-variance anomalies rather than identify them as outliers.
Wars are offered as an example of local SST anomalies without data, mechanism, or an outlier diagnostic.
Mean centering alone does not remove trend, seasonality, or nonstationarity before covariance estimation.
No standardization or area weighting is used, so variance magnitude rather than ecological relevance controls the modes.
The notation sums k to m modes even though the spatial covariance has at most n eigenvectors; here m and n differ.
No test shows that the centered full-field representation preserves coastal threshold crossings important to the fish maps.
The 680-by-680 covariance is estimated from at most 458 snapshots and is rank deficient after centering, but no SVD or regularization is discussed.
Eigenvectors are treated as uniquely stable without checking eigenvalue separation, sign convention, sampling uncertainty, or mode rotation.
The paper borrows kinetic-energy language from fluid POD even though the field is SST and the eigenvalues represent temperature variance.
No covariance residual, spatial correlation length, or comparison with snapshot-method POD is reported.
It is unclear whether the final modes use all 458 snapshots while the validation modes use only 446, and whether any reported error leaks test information.
No numerical eigensolver, precision, convergence, or reproducible eigenvector values are supplied.
Only three mode images are shown; the complete spatial arrays needed for future reconstruction are absent.
The first three printed proportions sum to 97.36 percent, while the prose rounds this to 97 percent without reporting the exact cumulative value.
A 2.64-percent global discarded variance can be concentrated near a 5, 7, 10, or 14 C habitat boundary, but no threshold-error test is performed.
The displayed decoding reconstructs centered D_prime; an absolute SST forecast still needs the mean field, which is omitted from the forecast formula.
No reconstruction RMSE, maximum local error, coastal error map, or held-out mode-count comparison supports choosing exactly three modes.
Explained variance is treated as effective information retention without quantifying the information relevant to critical-year decisions.
The coefficient matrix orientation and units are not documented in a downloadable table.
The central 50-year coefficient forecast has no displayed regression or Fourier equation in the paper.
No fitted intercepts, trends, frequencies, harmonic order, phases, amplitudes, or selection criterion are reported.
A 39-year historical record is extrapolated roughly 50 years without a long-horizon hindcast.
Linear trends are extended through 2070 without greenhouse-gas, ocean-circulation, or other climate forcing scenarios.
Fourier periodicity can reproduce seasonal cycles but does not establish the future persistence of interannual climate variability.
No residual autocorrelation, heteroskedasticity, spectral leakage, or breakpoint diagnostic is shown for any coefficient series.
Figure 2 provides no numerical forecast table or calibrated uncertainty band.
The first coefficient forecast visually continues a strong trend while the other coefficients are oscillatory, but no physical interpretation or bound is given.
The time scale alternates between monthly snapshots, plotted dates, and a 50-year statement without an explicit index convention.
The 12-month holdout assesses near-term extrapolation and cannot support the same accuracy label for 600 future months.
The fixed-mode reconstruction assumes spatial warming patterns never change over fifty years, despite the nonstationary climate premise.
No physical temperature bounds, conservation constraint, or comparison with a climate-model baseline is imposed.
The article's 3 C average warming near Scotland is not tabulated, spatially defined, or accompanied by uncertainty in the body.
Figure 3 shows selected future maps but no full annual/monthly fields needed to reproduce the fish envelopes.
Forecast uncertainty from modes, coefficient regression, truncation, and data error is not propagated downstream.
The 5-7 C herring and 10-14 C mackerel bands are transferred from cited habitat material without demonstrating Scottish stock, season, age, or life-stage applicability.
Temperature is the only habitat variable; salinity, depth, currents, oxygen, prey, spawning, fishing pressure, density, and interactions are omitted.
The red map regions are temperature-qualified cells, not observed population distribution, abundance, probability, or catch density.
The paper repeatedly calls independent yearly envelopes migration paths although no fish state is advanced from one year to the next.
No initial herring or mackerel distribution is used, so every qualifying cell is treated as a possible location regardless of reachability.
Only March herring and August mackerel are modeled; the official yearly distribution question and other fishing seasons are not resolved.
No observed Scottish species map validates the 2020 envelope before future maps are interpreted.
The contour maps have no probability scale, abundance legend, area summary, or uncertainty boundary.
Nonmonotone habitat area is noted for 2030 versus 2040 but is not traced to forecast uncertainty or modal behavior.
The public article says both species move east in the North Sea, while the Summary specifically attributes the eastward route only to herring.
TVB-N and K-value are spoilage or degradation indicators, not direct quantities of nutrient loss as the repeated model name suggests.
The first-order exponential law is adopted without fitting residuals or comparing alternative spoilage kinetics.
One constant storage temperature is assumed for a trip, with no time-temperature history, icing dynamics, handling, or ambient exposure.
The initial TVB-N and K values are treated as fixed across herring and mackerel without target-species measurements.
The source study concerns grass carp, so the kinetic and initial states are transferred across species, water, harvest, and handling regimes.
No microbial safety, sensory quality, histamine, oxidation, texture, or regulatory shelf-life mechanism is coupled to the two indicators.
The Arrhenius regressions appear to use very few temperature points, but sample size, replicates, measurement error, and fit statistics are absent.
The fitted lines report no confidence intervals for slope, intercept, activation energy, or frequency factor.
Table 4 omits the per-day units required for both frequency factors.
The fitted temperature range is not declared, yet sensitivity is later evaluated down to 250 K.
The printed -7037.9 slope and R=8.3144 imply Ea about 58515.9 J/mol, not Table 4's 58501.84; the K-value line has the same small ledger inconsistency.
The model assumes the same Arrhenius law remains valid through chilled, supercooled, and potentially frozen regimes.
No independent target-species holdout validates either rate law.
The logarithms are applied to dimensional indicator values without an explicit reference unit, making the written expressions formally unit-dependent.
The 30 mg/100g and 60-percent maxima are attributed only to unspecified national food standards.
Selecting the minimum of two indicator times ignores other safety or quality limits that could bind earlier.
Table 5 gives deterministic times with no parameter, measurement, individual, or temperature uncertainty.
The model calls the minimum t_rot but never defines whether the threshold means unsafe, unacceptable, or merely lower quality.
The reported storage times are treated as exact integer days when converted to range, despite values such as 3.89 and 2.54 days.
A vessel speed of 100 km/day is asserted without vessel, weather, route, or source evidence.
Fishing time, searching, gear deployment, handling, port operations, and contingency time are excluded from the freshness clock.
March 9 C and August 15 C are used as constant on-vessel storage temperatures without a measurement source or control model.
The Summary assigns 300 km and 500 km to herring and mackerel respectively, reversing the body's herring 500 km and mackerel 300 km.
One port at 57.69 N, -1.83 E represents all Scottish small fishing companies without a port distribution or fleet weights.
No geodesic or map-projection method defines the 300/500-km circles on the longitude-latitude figures.
The critical event is called tangency but the paper does not specify first contact, last contact, zero overlap, minimum abundance, or economic impracticality.
A temperature-qualified habitat area is treated as a fish population whose disappearance from a circle defines zero harvest.
No catch, effort, vessel capacity, quota, revenue, or profit threshold connects spatial overlap to company feasibility.
Storage time begins when fish are caught, but the route and harvest schedule used to interpret maximum distance are not stated.
Both temperature-preference distributions are called normal without any standard deviation, sample size, or source data.
The paper correctly states a 12 C mean for mackerel, then calls 6 C its most-likely value in the next paragraph.
The mackerel best/likely/worst values are described as about 7, 6, and 5 C, all inconsistent with its earlier 10-14 C band.
The worst-mackerel paragraph begins by saying herring could survive around 5 C, then reports a mackerel 2027 result.
No quantiles or probabilities define why the three selected temperatures are best, most likely, and worst.
The herring scenario values are not explicitly listed even though its table reports three dates.
No SST forecast uncertainty is combined with preference uncertainty, so the critical-year spread is incomplete.
The mackerel critical years inherit the species-temperature contradiction and cannot be reproduced as stated.
The no-critical-year best case is right-censored at 2070, not proof that no future threshold exists.
The Summary calls mackerel's no-critical-year outcome the worst case, while Table 6 clearly places it in the best-case column.
No observed historical migration or range-loss date calibrates the critical-year procedure.
CF_i is described as net cash inflow but populated with total gross mackerel sales revenue for the entire Scottish industry.
The calculation does not subtract status-quo revenue, fishing cost, operating cost, taxes, maintenance, or working capital to obtain incremental cash flow.
All 169 million GBP of annual revenue is credited to relocation for thirteen years even though some catch and revenue would exist without relocation.
Revenue is frozen at its 2018 nominal value with no catch decline, price, inflation, quota, demand, or discount-consistent escalation.
The thirteen-year benefit horizon is inferred from two habitat-overlap dates, not a revenue trajectory.
The model assumes eleven entirely new ports at 45 million GBP each rather than specifying which companies, assets, or existing ports relocate.
The World Bank project cost is used as a generic average without country, capacity, year, scope, or currency conversion.
The 8-percent alternative return is assumed without a company financing or risk basis.
The Summary's 65 million GBP per year is obtained by roughly dividing 840 million NPV by 13, not by calculating an equivalent annual annuity.
At 8 percent over thirteen years, 840.74 million GBP corresponds to an equivalent annual amount near 106.3 million GBP, exposing the Summary's annualization error.
The analysis considers mackerel revenue but does not include herring or other port-dependent fisheries.
Industry-level cash flows are presented as feasibility for capital-constrained small companies without allocation, financing, or liquidity tests.
The claim that partial relocation preserves NPV assumes benefits and costs scale exactly proportionally, ignoring fixed costs and economies of scale.
Job loss is acknowledged qualitatively but excluded from the decision rule despite the stated management-consortium audience.
A positive NPV under incomplete cash flows does not establish practical attractiveness versus the other two uncosted strategies.
The printed inverse Arrhenius denominator is ln(delta log A)-ln(k0 S), the negative of the algebraically correct order for positive absolute temperature.
The same sign reversal appears in both TVB-N and K-value inverse equations.
Figure 12 nevertheless reports positive 269-275 K values, so the plotted implementation cannot match the printed formulas as written.
S is not defined in the symbols, prose, or formula immediately around the cold-chain inversion.
A_T and A_K replace the earlier A_max notation without explicitly stating that the maxima are used.
The required temperatures approach or fall below water freezing, but freezing, ice fraction, product damage, energy, and equipment feasibility are omitted.
The paper optimizes the furthest fish distance without modeling catch abundance, route choice, or whether harvesting the edge is economically useful.
The body starts herring mode change in 2044 and mackerel shipping in 2046, while the Summary broadly says companies need to change mode in 2045.
No refrigeration purchase, fuel, maintenance, capacity, financing, crew, or installation schedule enters the strategy.
The annual distance series and complete temperature outputs are not published beyond four rows and one plot.
The proposed fishing-versus-shipping vessel proportion is never assigned, optimized, or linked to catch and transport capacity.
Rendezvous locations, transfer times, spoilage during transfer, supplies, fuel, crew, weather, and safety are omitted.
Fishing vessels are said not to require land support although shipping vessels must repeatedly connect them to ports.
Shetland is described as a high-sea or open-sea warehouse location even though it is inhabited UK land.
The example company coordinate is printed as -1.83 degrees 3E, an internally malformed longitude.
The paper mixes a negative longitude with an E suffix, so the sign convention for the representative port is internally inconsistent.
Warehouse construction, land, refrigeration, handling, throughput, lease-freight frequency, cost, and delay are not modeled.
The claimed ability to continue mackerel fishing until 2068 is not derived in Table 6, a warehouse equation, or a route table.
The warehouse paragraph switches between herring in the North Sea and mackerel in the north Atlantic without species-specific logistics.
No common cash-flow model compares transit stations with relocation or fleet refrigeration.
The new mode is presented as feasible without testing how many small firms can sacrifice vessels for non-fishing roles.
The official foreign-territorial-water proportion is never represented, varied, or reported.
The claim that all herring enters Danish territory in 2035 has no spatial overlay, table, equation, or area calculation.
The territorial revision compares a 2036 trigger with 2045 even though the baseline most-likely herring critical year is 2043.
Territorial seas, exclusive economic zones, quota access, licensing, bilateral rights, and Faroe administration are not distinguished.
The text treats the Danish Faroe Islands as adjacent to the proposed Shetland location and implies Danish waters surround Shetland.
Figure 13 is only credited to a homepage and is not converted into the model grid or a legal mask.
Figure 13 is labeled as an exclusive-economic-zone map, not a territorial-sea map, so it does not depict the legal regime named in the prose.
A one-degree SST grid is too coarse to resolve a 12-nautical-mile territorial sea without a finer geospatial layer.
No quantitative catch, cost, revenue, NPV, or loss result is recalculated under the restriction.
The Summary says the earlier change causes companies to lose money, but the body provides no loss amount or cash-flow equation.
The restricted scenario does not compare relocation, vessel split, and warehouse strategies on a common access basis.
Only initial TVB-N/K levels are perturbed; SST data, mode count, coefficient forecast, species preferences, speed, thresholds, economics, and legal access are fixed.
Three magnitudes times two directions produce six perturbation settings per indicator, so the claim of six equation sets is ambiguous when both indicators are modeled.
The output y and denominator used for relative error are not defined in the paper.
Sensitivity is extended to 250 K without showing that the Arrhenius calibration data cover that range.
The step-like relative-error curves can arise when the minimum switches between TVB-N and K-value, but the paper does not analyze the binding indicator.
Output changes similar to input changes are labeled robust without an acceptance threshold or decision-based criterion.
No critical-year, required-temperature, NPV, or strategy-ranking reversal is measured.
Initial-value stability cannot justify the claim that the model is universal to all fish in a species.
Individual variation in size, diet, environment, kinetics, thresholds, and handling is reduced to A0 alone.
No joint uncertainty, Monte Carlo propagation, structural alternative, or external validation is performed.
The public article's 3 C warming claim lacks a body table, location definition, uncertainty interval, or direct citation.
The article says the distribution changes little for five to ten years without a displayed metric or threshold supporting that planning window.
The article recommends relocation as a result while omitting the gross-revenue and incomplete-cost boundaries of the NPV.
The article recommends vessel refrigeration without disclosing the sign error, subfreezing requirements, or absent implementation costs.
The article again calls Shetland a high-sea warehouse area and presents the uncosted transit option as a way to obtain more catch.
Reference 5 merges a World Bank port-project entry with a second mackerel PDF URL, obscuring which source supports which quantity.
The Scottish Parliament mackerel revenue, 8-percent discount rate, eleven ports, and 45-million port average lack clean row-level source mapping.
No reference supplies the claimed normal preference variances because no variances are reported at all.
The territorial-water map source is not included as a complete bibliographic reference or licensed data layer.
The appendix publishes no POD modes, coefficient fits, Fourier settings, future SST arrays, code, or environment.
The appendix publishes no revenue rows, port-cost conversions, cash-flow schedule, or strategy calculations.
The appendix publishes no sensitivity input/output table despite the detailed percentage claims.
No executable mapping code or species data package supports the temperature-envelope figures.
A third-party MATHmodels Chinese QR/footer watermark appears throughout the paper and is not part of the team submission.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Compresses POD SST, species envelopes, freshness-limited range, critical years, three strategies, territorial change, and validation into six paragraphs.
Shows the requirement-ordered path from assumptions through four problem solutions, sensitivity, evaluation, and the public article.
Makes distribution, elapsed time, strategy feasibility, and territorial effects visible before modeling.
Lists the SST dataset, snapshot, spoilage indicator, absolute temperature, and storage time.
Defines snapshots, the dataset matrix, full modal expansion, centering, covariance, and eigenvectors.
Reports the first five eigenvalues and their shares, supporting the three-mode reduction.
Shows projection, full decoding, and the retained three-mode approximation.
Pairs three spatial fields with their time coefficient series.
Shows four of twelve monthly errors and states the 13.69-percent average.
Overlays historical and extrapolated trend-periodic paths for the three retained coefficients.
Shows selected regional future temperature fields through 2070.
Shows herring March and mackerel August qualifying cells over multiple future years.
Introduces a shared first-order model for TVB-N and K-value.
Plots log-rate against inverse temperature for the two indicators.
Reports frequency factors and activation energies for TVB-N and K-value.
Shows both indicators rising toward maximum accepted levels at several temperatures.
Compares TVB-N, K-value, and binding storage time for five temperatures.
Shows the rapid decline in acceptable time as temperature rises.
Presents best, most-likely, and worst outcomes for both species.
Overlays red species temperature envelopes with green port-centered fishing circles at scenario years.
Compares current-port 2045 and Shetland-port 2058 overlap maps.
Connects thirteen annual cash inflows, an 8-percent discount rate, and eleven port construction costs.
Lists four annual post-2043 herring distances around 969-1048 km.
Plots annual herring and mackerel cold-chain temperatures around 269-275 K.
Adds an externally sourced map to the qualitative Danish-water discussion without a computed overlay.
Shows storage-model outputs and relative responses for three symmetric perturbation sizes.
Balances three asserted strengths with two acknowledged limitations.
Uses four paragraphs to move from climate context through modeled findings to three adaptation options.
Lists ecology, POD, spoilage, quality, port, SST, and mackerel sources, including one malformed merged entry.
Publishes all holdout errors from 4.85 to 23.21 percent and the 13.69-percent mean.
